rows.question: What was Apple's total net sales (revenue) for fiscal year 2023, the fiscal year ended September 30, 2023?
rows.answer:
Apple's total net sales for fiscal year 2023 (the 52 weeks from 2022-09-25 to 2023-09-30) were **$383,285,000,000**, about $383.3 billion.

This comes from the XBRL tag `RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax`. The tool returned it with Apple's fiscal 2025 10-K (accession 0000320193-25-000079), which also reports fiscal 2023 as a comparative year. I didn't open Apple's original fiscal 2023 10-K.

Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000032019325000079/0000320193-25-000079-index.htm

```json
{"values": {"AAPL FY2023 revenue": 383285000000}}
```

rows.question: Compare Nvidia's and AMD's revenue growth from fiscal year 2022 to fiscal year 2024 (Nvidia's fiscal years end in late January, so FY2024 ended January 28, 2024; AMD's FY2024 ended December 28, 2024). Give each company's FY2024 revenue and its total percentage revenue growth from FY2022 to FY2024.
rows.answer:
Nvidia's revenue grew far faster than AMD's from FY2022 to FY2024. Nvidia grew 126.4% and AMD grew 9.3%.

| | FY2022 revenue | FY2024 revenue | Growth FY2022–FY2024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nvidia | $26,914,000,000 (year ended Jan 30, 2022) | $60,922,000,000 (year ended Jan 28, 2024) | 126.4% |
| AMD | $23,601,000,000 (year ended Dec 31, 2022) | $25,785,000,000 (year ended Dec 28, 2024) | 9.3% |

I calculated growth as (FY2024 / FY2022 − 1) × 100, using the revenue figures from SEC XBRL data.

- **Nvidia:** 60,922 / 26,914 − 1 gives 126.4%. Sources: [FY2024 figure](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000021/0001045810-26-000021-index.htm) and [FY2022 figure](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581024000029/0001045810-24-000029-index.htm).
- **AMD:** 25,785 / 23,601 − 1 gives 9.3%. Sources: [FY2024 figure](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2488/000000248826000018/0000002488-26-000018-index.htm) and [FY2022 figure](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2488/000000248825000012/0000002488-25-000012-index.htm).

The two fiscal years end at different times, so the periods are not perfectly aligned. Nvidia's FY2024 ended in January 2024, about 11 months before AMD's FY2024.


rows.question: What was Tesla's net income in fiscal year 2023 and in fiscal year 2024, and by what percentage did it change from FY2023 to FY2024?
rows.answer:
Tesla's net income attributable to common stockholders fell from $14,997,000,000 in FY2023 to $7,091,000,000 in FY2024. That is a 52.7% decline.

- **FY2023:** $14,997,000,000, for the year ended 2023-12-31.
- **FY2024:** $7,091,000,000, for the year ended 2024-12-31.
- **Change:** (7,091 / 14,997 − 1) × 100 = −52.7%.

Both figures come from the XBRL data for Tesla's net income (loss) attributable to parent. The filing that returned them is accession 0001628280-26-003952, which is the FY2025 10-K filed 2026-01-29. I did not open the FY2023 and FY2024 10-Ks themselves.

Sources: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828026003952/0001628280-26-003952-index.htm and https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyfacts/CIK0001318605.json

```json

```

rows.question: According to Item 1 (Business) of Nvidia's Form 10-K for fiscal year 2024 (fiscal year ended January 28, 2024), in how many segments does Nvidia report its business results?
rows.answer:
Nvidia reports its business results in **two segments**. Item 1 of its fiscal year 2024 Form 10-K says: "We report our business results in two segments." The two segments are:
- **Compute & Networking.** This covers Data Center accelerated computing platforms, networking, the DRIVE automated-driving platform, Jetson robotics and embedded platforms, and NVIDIA AI Enterprise and other software.
- **Graphics.** This covers GeForce GPUs, GeForce NOW, Quadro/RTX workstation GPUs, and vGPU software.

Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581024000029/nvda-20240128.htm (accession 0001045810-24-000029)


rows.question: According to Item 1 of Microsoft's Form 10-K for fiscal year 2024, approximately how many people did Microsoft employ full-time as of June 30, 2024?
rows.answer:
Microsoft's fiscal year 2024 Form 10-K says that "As of June 30, 2024, we employed approximately 228,000 people on a full-time basis." The Human Capital Resources section of Item 1 gives the breakdown:

- **By location:** 126,000 in the U.S. and 102,000 internationally.
- **By function:** 86,000 in operations, 81,000 in product research and development, 45,000 in sales and marketing, and 16,000 in general and administration.

Source: [Microsoft 10-K for fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, accession 0000950170-24-087843](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000095017024087843/msft-20240630.htm)
